answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost.
